profiles.subject: Theotokos

overview.text: The Vladimir icon presents the Mother of God and Christ with their faces touching. The displayed historical image is the widely reproduced Vladimir work, rather than an interchangeable portrait of Mary or a generic image of mother and child.

blocks.text: Christ reaches around his mother’s neck while she inclines her face toward him. The worn historical painted surface is visible. The source identifies the work as the Virgin of Vladimir; the reproduction is retained without restoration or added details.

blocks.text: The OCA’s account attributes the prototype to Saint Luke within Church tradition. It records the icon’s arrival from Constantinople in 1131, its transfer to Vladimir in 1155 and its first arrival in Moscow in 1395. Traditional authorship should be distinguished from the surviving object’s art-historical identification.

blocks.text: The August 26 commemoration concerns the meeting of the icon in Moscow. The OCA connects it with the city’s deliverance from Tamerlane and relates a vision of the Mother of God as part of that Church narrative.
